records.real_world_identity_notes: PMR identifies this entry as the 2013 Holden Commodore VF. Official COTF and Albins evidence establishes a six-speed sequential dog-ring transaxle, manual stick actuation, and mandated upshift shift-cut behavior. Exact 2013 wheel hardware and detailed driver technique remain open.

records.specification_basis: COTF and Albins sources establish the six-speed transaxle. The official COTF report discusses dog-ring wear in the control transaxle. The ST6 manufacturer documentation establishes sequential rod/cable activation and the COTF installation is the manual-stick system. The ST6 is documented as sequential. The six-speed sequential race transmission uses a driver-operated clutch for standing starts; no automatic launch system was established. The mandated shift-cut system is explicitly intended to reduce shift loads during rapid wide-open-throttle gear changes. The documented shift cut momentarily interrupts torque and supports wide-open-throttle upshifts. Official COTF documentation describes mandated shift-cut settings. Dog-ring race transmission construction supports clutchless downshift as the hardware baseline; exact driver technique remains reviewable. Dog-ring construction establishes the mechanism; manual rev matching is the derived downshift technique unless an automatic blip is separately established. The reviewed sources did not establish the remaining technique and wheel fields, which stay unknown in the real-car baseline: /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/manual_blip, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/automatic_blip, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/throttle_lift, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/automatic_cut, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/automatic_blip, /authentic_controls/steering/wheel_rim/shape, /authentic_controls/steering/wheel_rim/integrated_display, /authentic_controls/steering/wheel_rim/shift_lights, /authentic_controls/steering/wheel_rim/open_top.
